summary: Credible bottom-up wedge (free IaC scanner in CI) and a sharp first-customer trigger (SOC 2 audit), but the $10/resource/month price is orders of magnitude off native tooling and would produce six-figure bills for mid-size accounts. Running OSS self-serve and CISO direct sales at once with 15 people, and an undecided budget owner, strain the motion.

objections.objection: Per-resource price is mis-set: $10/resource/month means a modest 3,000-resource estate costs ~$360k/yr, far above what a 100-500 person SaaS firm without a security team budgets, while AWS Config charges fractions of a cent per resource evaluation. Resource counting (IAM roles, security groups, ephemeral resources) also invites bill shock and customers excluding accounts.

Two sales motions at once: OSS community feeding self-serve plus direct CISO sales. The named first customers have small or no security teams, so the CISO buyer often does not exist; the concept itself lists 'who owns the budget: engineering or security?' as open. Without a decided buyer, messaging, pricing page and sales comp split.

Free OSS scanner may capture most of the value (PR-time checks) for the target segment; the paid tier's value (runtime drift, remediation PRs, compliance mapping) overlaps free Cloud Custodian and cloud-native posture checks, so conversion rates may be low.
Riskiest-assumption test runs only 2 weeks and counts repositories and inbound requests, not paid conversions or willingness to pay at the stated price; it cannot validate pricing.

No packaging for the compliance buyer (SOC 2/PCI report bundles, fixed per-account or per-tier pricing) even though compliance is named as the reason to pay; enterprise incumbents sell quote-based annual contracts that procurement understands.

strongest_point: Free CI scanner gives zero-friction engineer adoption and usage data, and SOC 2-bound startups are a concrete, urgent first-customer segment whose spend grows with cloud footprint.
what_would_change_my_mind: A tiered price (per cloud account or resource bands, roughly $1-3k/month for a mid-size estate) accepted by 5 of the first 10 design partners as signed paid pilots.
OSS-to-paid conversion of at least 2-3% of active organizations within a quarter.
A decision that engineering (VP Eng/platform) is the primary budget owner, with a self-serve-to-sales-assist motion.
